goals.description: If medication is started and absence of CKD is verified, complete the follow-up BMP at 4 weeks to assess renal function and electrolytes.
If medication is started and CKD is confirmed, complete the follow-up BMP at 2 weeks to assess renal function and electrolytes.

Perform structured home BP monitoring with two readings one minute apart each morning before medication and two readings one minute apart each evening, on at least 3 and preferably 7 consecutive days; submit readings weekly for weekly average review and threshold assessment.
Review the seven-day home BP average 2 to 4 weeks after starting or changing medication, separately from laboratory follow-up.
Have each submitted weekly home BP series reviewed by the care team within 7 days of submission.
For a home BP reading above 180/120 mmHg, repeat the measurement after 5 minutes and contact the clinic the same day if the repeat remains above that threshold.
Send a reminder after a week without home readings; if readings remain absent after 3 reminder attempts on different days, complete direct contact to identify monitoring barriers.
Maintain a documented BP reading within the preceding 12 months.
Receive lifestyle modification education materials at hypertension diagnosis; verify whether this has already occurred because the diagnosis date and prior education are unavailable.
Adopt a DASH dietary pattern and restrict sodium intake to strictly less than 2300 mg/day.
Achieve at least 150 minutes/week of moderate-intensity aerobic activity or at least 75 minutes/week of vigorous-intensity aerobic activity.
Achieve and maintain BMI within 18.5 to 24.9 kg/m2. Assess current BMI before determining whether weight change is indicated; do not assume excess weight.

If alcohol is consumed, establish applicability before selecting a patient-specific limit. Preserve the source branches: no more than 2 drinks/day for men and no more than 1 drink/day for women. No patient-specific branch is selected.
If smoking is identified, support smoking cessation with counseling and resources, with a target of no smoking. Smoking status is not established.

One medication initiation goal covers the applicable criteria: (Complete clinician assessment and initiate the recommended pharmacotherapy within 30 days of meeting treatment criteria. Confirm the unspecified medication route before prescription release. No numerical treatment BP target is provided in the supplied recommendations) OR (Complete the treatment-decision follow-up 2 weeks after medication initiation).

activities.description: Complete prescribing-clinician assessment for the recommended lisinopril regimen. Confirm the administration route, actual treatment start, and renal disease status before releasing a prescription or selecting a laboratory branch. As a supplemental medication-safety assessment, review baseline creatinine/eGFR and potassium; arrange assessment of unavailable baseline results before finalizing the prescription. This baseline assessment is not an additional source-defined follow-up schedule.
activities.frequency: Before prescription release
activities.clinicalRationale: Supports the timely pharmacotherapy and renal-safety goals. DMN call indices are zero-based. Treatment call 2 recommends initiation, but no route is supplied. Has Kidney Disease=false resulted from a definitive miss and does not establish clinical absence of CKD. Baseline laboratory review is a supplemental safety consideration requested by the reviewer, not a quoted requirement of the supplied CPG. No terminology lookup results were supplied, so all terminology fields remain null.

activities.description: Proposed regimen: start lisinopril 10 mg once daily after prescribing-clinician assessment. This activity is not an executable prescription until the administration route is supplied and confirmed.
activities.route: Unspecified in supplied recommendations; prescribing-clinician confirmation required before prescription release
activities.frequency: Once daily
activities.clinicalRationale: Supports timely pharmacotherapy. Treatment DMN used SBP 142 mmHg, diabetes=true, and kidney disease=false and returned lisinopril 10 mg daily with 2-week follow-up. Applicable criteria are SBP >=130 mmHg with diabetes and the independent principle of SBP >=140 mmHg regardless of comorbidity. Identical same-CPG regimens are consolidated with all three recommendation IDs. Kidney status remains subject to verification. Failed classification and confirmation DMNs do not establish an office BP category or sufficient measurement occasions.

activities.description: Track ACE inhibitor follow-up laboratory completion against the selected renal-status branch and document responsible-clinician review of results.
activities.frequency: For each ACE inhibitor initiation: assess completion at the applicable 4-week or 2-week deadline
activities.clinicalRationale: Supports the branch-specific BMP completion goals and timely laboratory quality measure without creating a third laboratory schedule.

activities.description: Use a validated upper-arm BP device. Take two readings one minute apart in the morning before medications and two readings one minute apart in the evening on at least 3 and preferably 7 consecutive days. Transmit readings weekly through the patient portal, secure messaging, or telephone; the care team calculates and reviews average systolic and diastolic BP.
activities.frequency: Two morning and two evening readings on at least 3, preferably 7, consecutive days; transmission and average review weekly
activities.clinicalRationale: Implements the structured home-monitoring goal because a Table 1 treatment decision has been made. Missing office classification inputs do not supply home measurements or negate this recommendation.

activities.description: At weekly home-average review, interpret a home average of 135/85 mmHg or higher as equivalent to office BP 140/90 mmHg. Notify the responsible clinician routinely when average systolic BP is >=135 mmHg or average diastolic BP is >=85 mmHg, or when a lower clinician-set diabetes or CKD threshold is exceeded. No lower patient-specific threshold has been supplied.
activities.frequency: At each weekly home-average review
activities.clinicalRationale: Supports the home-monitoring and threshold-assessment goal. These are interpretation and notification thresholds, not source-defined treatment targets. Diabetes permits a clinician-set lower threshold but does not supply its value.

activities.description: Review the seven-day home systolic and diastolic BP average 2 to 4 weeks after medication initiation or change.
activities.frequency: Once 2 to 4 weeks after each medication initiation or change
activities.clinicalRationale: Implements the distinct post-change home-average review goal. This source-defined 2-to-4-week window is additional to BMP follow-up and remains distinct from the treatment DMN's 2-week follow-up.

activities.clinicalRationale: Implements the seven-day submission-review goal. This quality deadline is measured from submission, not from medication initiation.

activities.description: If a single home systolic BP is >180 mmHg or diastolic BP is >120 mmHg, repeat BP after 5 minutes. If repeat systolic BP remains >180 mmHg or diastolic BP remains >120 mmHg, contact the clinic the same day.
activities.frequency: Event-triggered: repeat after 5 minutes; same-day clinic contact if the repeat remains above the threshold
activities.clinicalRationale: Implements the conditional severe-reading response goal. Call 4 failed because initial and repeat BP values were missing; no severe episode or reassuring repeat can be inferred. Timing and criteria are preserved from the recommendation rather than attributed to a successful DMN output.

activities.description: If one week passes without home readings, send a reminder. If readings remain absent after three reminder attempts on different days, contact the patient directly to identify barriers. Record reminder dates, attempts, and whether readings were received.
activities.frequency: Reminder after 1 week without readings; direct contact after 3 unsuccessful reminder attempts on different days
activities.clinicalRationale: Implements the conditional outreach goal. Call 5 failed because the reminder-attempt count was missing. Its definitive-miss false inputs do not establish actual submission history or negate the proposed medication initiation. No immediate outreach is asserted without confirming the trigger.

activities.description: Verify that the hypertension record contains a dated BP reading within the preceding 12 months and arrange BP documentation if the measure is unmet.
activities.frequency: Assess against the preceding 12-month documentation window; audit cadence is not specified by the source
activities.clinicalRationale: Supports the BP-documentation goal. SBP 142 appears in the treatment inputs, but the underlying observation date is not supplied here, so satisfaction of the 12-month quality measure cannot be assumed.

activities.description: Provide lifestyle-modification education materials at hypertension diagnosis. Verify whether diagnosis-time education has already been completed; if not, provide the materials and document delivery.
activities.frequency: At diagnosis; verify prior completion because diagnosis timing is unavailable
activities.clinicalRationale: Supports the education-delivery goal without assuming that hypertension was newly diagnosed or that prior education was omitted.

activities.description: Counsel on adopting a DASH dietary pattern emphasizing fruits, vegetables, whole grains, and low-fat dairy products while limiting saturated fat and keeping sodium intake strictly below 2300 mg/day.
activities.frequency: Daily dietary practice; counseling repetition interval is not specified
activities.clinicalRationale: Supports the DASH and sodium goal. The source recommends lifestyle counseling for all patients with hypertension, including those receiving medication.

activities.description: Counsel on at least 150 minutes/week of moderate-intensity aerobic exercise, such as brisk walking, or at least 75 minutes/week of vigorous-intensity aerobic exercise.
activities.frequency: At least 150 minutes/week moderate intensity or 75 minutes/week vigorous intensity
activities.clinicalRationale: Supports the measurable physical-activity goal as an adjunct to medication, preserving both source-defined exercise alternatives.

activities.description: Assess current weight and BMI and counsel on achieving and maintaining BMI 18.5 to 24.9 kg/m2. If weight loss is clinically indicated after assessment, discuss the source-described BP benefit of 5% to 10% weight loss; do not prescribe weight loss solely from the available demographics.
activities.frequency: Ongoing weight-management practice; reassessment interval is not specified
activities.clinicalRationale: Supports the healthy-BMI goal while preserving uncertainty about baseline BMI and whether weight loss is appropriate.

activities.description: Assess whether alcohol is consumed and establish which source branch applies before selecting a patient-specific limit. If alcohol is consumed, counsel conditionally on no more than 2 drinks/day for men and no more than 1 drink/day for women. Do not assign either branch from the supplied name or demographic label.
activities.frequency: Daily intake limits only if alcohol is consumed and branch applicability is established
activities.clinicalRationale: Supports the conditional alcohol goal. Alcohol use and the information needed to establish branch applicability have not been verified; both source limits remain conditional and no patient-specific 2-drink target is assigned.

activities.description: Establish smoking status. If smoking is present, provide cessation counseling and cessation resources to support stopping smoking.
activities.frequency: Conditional on smoking; counseling repetition interval is not specified
activities.clinicalRationale: Supports the conditional smoking-cessation goal without inferring tobacco use. The source explicitly limits cessation counseling to applicable patients.

description.text: If medication is started and absence of CKD is verified, complete the follow-up BMP at 4 weeks to assess renal function and electrolytes.
If medication is started and CKD is confirmed, complete the follow-up BMP at 2 weeks to assess renal function and electrolytes.

Perform structured home BP monitoring with two readings one minute apart each morning before medication and two readings one minute apart each evening, on at least 3 and preferably 7 consecutive days; submit readings weekly for weekly average review and threshold assessment.
Review the seven-day home BP average 2 to 4 weeks after starting or changing medication, separately from laboratory follow-up.
Have each submitted weekly home BP series reviewed by the care team within 7 days of submission.
For a home BP reading above 180/120 mmHg, repeat the measurement after 5 minutes and contact the clinic the same day if the repeat remains above that threshold.
Send a reminder after a week without home readings; if readings remain absent after 3 reminder attempts on different days, complete direct contact to identify monitoring barriers.
Maintain a documented BP reading within the preceding 12 months.
Receive lifestyle modification education materials at hypertension diagnosis; verify whether this has already occurred because the diagnosis date and prior education are unavailable.
Adopt a DASH dietary pattern and restrict sodium intake to strictly less than 2300 mg/day.
Achieve at least 150 minutes/week of moderate-intensity aerobic activity or at least 75 minutes/week of vigorous-intensity aerobic activity.
Achieve and maintain BMI within 18.5 to 24.9 kg/m2. Assess current BMI before determining whether weight change is indicated; do not assume excess weight.

If alcohol is consumed, establish applicability before selecting a patient-specific limit. Preserve the source branches: no more than 2 drinks/day for men and no more than 1 drink/day for women. No patient-specific branch is selected.
If smoking is identified, support smoking cessation with counseling and resources, with a target of no smoking. Smoking status is not established.
